subject: Zooming: avoid clipping with untouched unevenly spaced log10 gridlines

messages.author: a9b714c5bcaebd1e
messages.subject: Zooming: avoid clipping with untouched unevenly spaced log10 gridlines
parts:
Hello all,

I have a spectrum with unevenly space vertical gridlines in log10.

freq <- 10^seq(2, 4, by  = 0.1)
d <- rnorm(length(freq))
data <- data.frame(freq, d)

ggplot(data = data, aes(x = freq, y = d)) + coord_trans(x = "log10") + geom_line() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1000*seq(1,10,by = 2))

My objective is to zoom into a certain region of the plot.

scale_x_continuous() shows clipping removing unseen data points. However, the vertical gridlines are not changed:

ggplot(data = data, aes(x = freq, y = d)) + coord_trans(x = "log10") + geom_line() +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(3000, 8000), breaks = 1000*seq(1,10,by = 2))

There is no clipping with coord_cartesian(), but the vertical gridlines got modified and evenly spaced:

ggplot(data = data, aes(x = freq, y = d)) + coord_trans(x = "log10") + geom_line() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1000*seq(1,10,by = 2)) + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(3000, 8000))

How can I avoid both clipping and keep the original unevenly spaced log10 vertical gridlines?

Thanks.

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Zooming: avoid clipping with untouched unevenly spaced log10 gridlines
parts:
I have no idea if this is what you want, but here's one attempt:

dat <- data.frame(freq = 10^seq(2, 4, by = 0.1),
d = rnorm(length(freq)))


library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
dat %>% filter(freq > 3000 & freq < 8000) %>%
ggplot(., aes(x = freq, y = d)) +

scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1000*seq(2, 8))

All I did was pre-select the data in the desired region and then
construct the plot as usual. This is one way to avoid clipping and
maintain the log scaling on the x-axis.

One thing to remember in ggplot2: scale transformation precedes
statistical transformation, which in turn precedes coordinate
transformation. coord_cartesian() uses a Cartesian coordinate system,
which is equally spaced. It overrode the log10 coordinate scaling
specified first. You're allowed one scale and one coordinate system
for each axis - if you specify a second one, it overrides the first
(often with a warning). This is why the log10 scaling got converted to
linear scaling on the x-axis in your third call.

Dennis
